newsitem.title: DEMOCRATIC REPUBLIC OF CONGO: Two mortar bombs hit Kinshasa, witnesses.
newsitem.headline: Two mortar bombs hit Kinshasa, witnesses.

text.p: Two mortar bombs landed in Kinshasa on Thursday, presumably fired from Republic of Congo across the river, witnesses said.
No one was hurt in the incident following a flareup of ethnic and political fighting in Brazzaville, capital of Republic of Congo.
"One of the bombs landed in the garden of a primary school near the foreign ministry," one witness said. The second fell in the middle of an empty road. Neither caused any material damage.

Earlier on Thursday, state radio in Democratic Republic of the Congo (formerly Zaire) said President Laurent Kabila's troops retataliated with mortar fire into Brazzaville after shells were fired from there on Tuesday.

Meanwhile hundreds of refugees crossed into Kinshasa on Thursday, fleeing renewed fighting in Brazzaville between forces loyal to President Pascal Lisouba and the militia of former military ruler Denis Sassou Nguesso.
The two sides have been battling since June and international mediation has so far yielded no breakthrough.
